case_name: Kerala State Toddy Shop Contractors Association v T. N. Prathapan, MLA and others
petitioner: Kerala State Toddy Shop Contractors Association
facts: The Kerala State Toddy Shop Contractors Association filed a public interest litigation before the High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam, highlighting the grievance that the licensed premises for sale of liquor were required to remain closed on certain days specified in Rule 28A of the Foreign Liquor (Compounding, Blending and Bottling) Rules, 1975.

The State of Kerala and its functionaries had issued orders allowing the sale of Indian Made Foreign Liquor ('IMFL' for short) on September 1, 2009, which was not legitimate in law and totally unlawful.

The High Court referred to Rule 28A of the Rules and took note of Section 71 of the Kerala Abkari Act and opined that unless the Rules are amended, the Government is bound to direct the IMFL shops to be closed on September 1, 2009.
issues: Whether the High Court can declare another rule as unconstitutional without any challenge to the same and further without impleading the affected parties even in representative capacity.
Whether the State Government has power to issue a notification under Section 71 of the Act to overlook the date specified in Rule 28A of the Rules.
petitioner_arguments: There was no pleading in that regard and no relief was sought on that score.

The seminal issue for consideration is whether, while interpreting the effect and impact of a particular rule relating to a different sphere, the High Court in exercise of its power under Article 226 of the Constitution can declare another rule as unconstitutional without any challenge to the same and further without impleading the affected parties even in representative capacity.
respondent_arguments: The Government has power to issue notification under Section 71 of the Act.
There was no pleading that the Rule upon which the reliance was placed by the respondent was ultra vires the Railways Act, 1890.
court_reasoning: The High Court fell into grave error by declaring another rule as discriminatory and unreasonable.
Suo motu assumption of jurisdiction in this regard is totally uncalled for and, therefore, that makes the judgment and order declaring the 2003 Rules as discriminatory sensitively susceptible.
It is a settled principle of law that a person who assails a provision to be ultra vires must plead the same in proper perspective.
holding: The appeals are allowed and the judgment and order of the High Court, as far as it declares the 2002 Rules as ultra vires in respect of the toddy shops being kept open on the first day of all English Calendar month is set aside.
There shall be no order as to costs.
